title: Health and Safety Before Service
introduction:
I use this page like a preflight card: check the hazards before the tools leave the drawer. Start with the general warnings, then read the precautions for the system you plan to work on. A stopped engine, a quiet fan or an apparently inactive electrical component does not necessarily mean the stored energy is gone.

The system sections apply to the technology, equipment and task named in each warning. Check what the vehicle actually has before choosing a section. This is a safety overview; use the matching workshop procedure for access, fan isolation, fuel-pressure release, restraint-system preparation, specified fluids, tightening torques and the repair itself. The precautions below do not supply those complete procedures.

items.name: Auto start-stop, where equipped
items.detail: WARNING: A vehicle with engine auto start-stop technology can start automatically with the ignition on. Switch the ignition off before servicing or working close to rotating engine parts. Failure to do so may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Keep control of the key
items.detail: WARNING: Remove the key from the vehicle to prevent another person from starting the engine during service. An accidental start may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Liquid refrigerant
items.detail: WARNING: Liquid R-134a and R-1234yf can injure eyes and freeze skin. Always wear safety goggles and avoid contact with liquid refrigerant. Failure to do so may cause serious personal injury. Read the [climate-control precautions](#/document/G1693184) before this work.

items.name: Refrigerant gas and flames
items.detail: WARNING: R-134a and R-1234yf gases can displace breathable air in confined spaces and produce toxic gases when burned at high temperatures. Do not release a large quantity in a confined space or expose the gas to a high-temperature flame, such as a torch. Consult the Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS). Failure to follow these precautions may cause serious personal injury or death.

items.name: Recovery and charging equipment
items.detail: WARNING: Use extreme care with refrigerants and observe every safety and service precaution on the refrigerant tank and recovery and charging equipment. Failure to do so may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Heater water hoses
items.detail: WARNING: Before disconnecting any heater water hose, shut the engine OFF and wait until it is fully cool. Escaping hot cooling-system liquid can cause burns or serious injury.

items.name: Electric booster heater, where fitted and being serviced
items.detail: WARNING: Allow the electric booster heater enough time to cool before servicing it. It can become hot enough during use to burn unprotected skin. Failure to allow cooling may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Sulfuric acid and explosive gases
items.detail: WARNING: Batteries containing sulfuric acid also produce explosive gases. Work in a well-ventilated area, keep flames, sparks and burning substances away, and avoid acid contact with skin, eyes and clothing. Shield your eyes against acid splashes when working nearby. If acid contacts skin or eyes, immediately flush with water for a minimum of 15 minutes, then obtain prompt medical attention. If swallowed, call a physician immediately. Failure to follow these instructions may cause serious personal injury. Read the [battery and charging precautions](#/document/G1693181).

items.name: Lift a plastic-cased battery without squeezing it
items.detail: WARNING: Use a battery carrier or place your hands on opposite corners. Excessive pressure on the end walls can force acid through the vent caps, causing personal injury and/or damage to the vehicle or battery.

items.name: Reconnect the battery vent
items.detail: WARNING: Whenever the battery vent tube has been disconnected, reconnect it properly afterward. Otherwise, harmful gases can enter the cabin and cause serious personal injury or death.

items.name: Wash after handling battery hardware
items.detail: WARNING: Battery posts, terminals and related accessories contain lead and lead components. Wash your hands after handling them. Failure to do so may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Li-ion batteries: explosion and fire hazard
items.detail: WARNING: Li-ion Battery terminals are always live, creating an explosion and fire hazard. Never place items or tools on the battery. Avoid short circuits and excessive discharge/charge rates. Use insulated tools only, and remove metallic items such as watches, bracelets and rings. Failure to follow these precautions may cause a fire or serious personal injury.

items.name: Li-ion battery case and electrolyte
items.detail: WARNING: Never try to open or disassemble a Li-ion Battery. Its electrolyte is very corrosive and is normally inaccessible under normal working conditions. If the case is damaged, do not touch exposed electrolyte or powder. Failure to follow these instructions may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Use clean, specified brake fluid
items.detail: WARNING: Use only clean brake fluid meeting the manufacturer's specification. Never reuse previously drained brake fluid. These restrictions help prevent system contamination, brake-component damage and serious personal injury. Read the [brake and clutch precautions](#/document/G1693183); obtain the actual fluid specification from the matching service information.

items.name: Control friction-component dust
items.detail: WARNING: Do not breathe the dust or use compressed air to blow it from storage containers or friction components. Remove it using government-approved techniques. Repairing brake pads, clutch discs and other friction components can release hazardous dust associated with cancer and lung disease. Exposure can also irritate skin, eyes and the respiratory tract, cause allergic reactions and/or lead to other chronic health effects. Seek medical attention or advice if irritation persists. Failure to follow these instructions may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Brake fluid on paint
items.detail: NOTICE: If brake fluid spills onto paintwork, immediately wash the affected area with cold water.

items.name: Chemical protection
items.detail: WARNING: Consult the Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS) whenever handling chemicals and wear the protective equipment it directs, which may include respirators and chemically resistant gloves. Failure to do so may cause serious personal injury. Read the [body-repair precautions](#/document/G1693182).

items.name: Sanding and grinding
items.detail: WARNING: Always wear protective equipment, including eye protection with side shields and a dust mask, when sanding or grinding. Failure to do so may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Protect hinge and striker anchoring areas
items.detail: WARNING: Do not perform body-side sectioning repairs in door-hinge or striker anchoring areas. Welding within 50 mm (1.96 in) of a door hinge or striker location can compromise structural integrity in a collision and cause serious injury to vehicle occupants.

items.name: Welding radiation
items.detail: WARNING: Welding emits invisible ultraviolet and infrared rays that can injure unprotected eyes and skin. Always use suitable protection, including a welding helmet with dark filter lenses of the correct density and protective clothing. Electric welding produces intense radiation; filter plate lenses of the deepest shade that still provides adequate visibility are recommended. Flash safety goggles are strongly recommended for people working in the weld area. Failure to follow these precautions may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Safety belts after a collision
items.detail: WARNING: Every collision repair must include inspection and correction of all safety belt components using Safety Belt Inspection and Repair After a Collision in Section 501-20A General Procedures. That separate procedure remains required; this overview does not supply its inspection and repair instructions. Omitting it may cause incorrect belt-system operation and increase the risk of serious personal injury or death in a crash. This requirement also appears in the [pyrotechnic-device precautions](#/document/G1693191).

items.name: RCM and impact-sensor mountings after a crash
items.detail: WARNING: Inspect the Restraints Control Module (RCM) and impact-sensor mounting areas for damage or deformation, and inspect related components for cracks, damage and loose fasteners. Restore damaged mounting areas to their original production configuration. After repairing a mounting area, replace the original RCM or impact sensor at that location with a new component, whether or not the airbags deployed. Failure to follow these instructions may cause serious personal injury or death in a crash.

items.name: Collision repair methods and replacement parts
items.detail: WARNING: Collision repairs must follow the workshop manual and use new, genuine Ford Motor Company replacement parts. Ford does not authorize recycled, salvaged, aftermarket or reconditioned replacements, including body parts, wheels and safety-restraint components. Alternate repair methods or substitute components can compromise structural integrity and crash-safety performance, potentially causing serious personal injury to occupants in a crash.

items.name: Let the engine cool before opening
items.detail: WARNING: Always allow the engine to cool before opening the cooling system. Never unscrew the coolant pressure relief cap while the engine is operating or the system is hot. Even slightly loosening the cap can release pressurized steam and hot liquid forcefully, causing serious personal injury. Read the [engine-cooling precautions](#/document/G1693187).

items.name: Release pressure before disturbing the system
items.detail: WARNING: Relieve fuel-system pressure before working on or disconnecting any fuel tube or fuel-system component. Fuel remains under high pressure even with the engine stopped and can spray accidentally, causing serious personal injury. Use the matching pressure-release procedure together with the [gasoline and gasoline-ethanol precautions](#/document/G1693188).

items.name: Keep tobacco and flames away
items.detail: WARNING: Do not smoke, carry lighted tobacco or have an open flame of any kind when working on or near fuel-related components. Highly flammable mixtures are always present and can ignite, causing serious personal injury.

items.name: Clean up before restarting
items.detail: WARNING: Remove all fuel residue from the engine compartment before returning the engine to operation. Remaining residue can ignite and cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Leave personal electronics outside the work area
items.detail: WARNING: Do not carry cell phones, pagers, audio equipment or other personal electronic devices when working on or near fuel-related components. Highly flammable mixtures are always present and can ignite, causing serious personal injury.

items.name: Disconnect the battery ground for fuel or EVAP service
items.detail: WARNING: Always disconnect the battery ground cable at the battery when working on an evaporative emission (EVAP) system or fuel-related component. Highly flammable mixtures are always present and can ignite, causing serious personal injury.

items.name: Prepare for spilled fuel
items.detail: WARNING: Observe fuel-handling precautions and prepare for possible spillage before handling fuel. Hot vehicle components and other ignition sources can ignite spilled fuel, causing serious personal injury.

items.name: Listen while loosening the filler cap
items.detail: WARNING: Remove the fuel filler cap slowly. If it vents vapor or you hear hissing, wait until that stops before removing the cap completely. Pressure can otherwise spray fuel out and cause serious personal injury. This cap-opening precaution does not replace the required fuel-system pressure-release procedure.

items.name: Running leak checks and high-pressure fuel
items.detail: WARNING: Avoid fuel contact during any visual fuel-leak inspection with the engine running. Do not work on the fuel system until pressure has been released and the engine has cooled. High-pressure fuel is hot and under very high pressure: it can cause cuts, while hot fuel can cause burns. Failure to follow these precautions may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Pressure and temperature before service
items.detail: WARNING: Do not work on a diesel fuel system until its pressure has been released and the engine has cooled. Fuel in the high-pressure system is hot and under very high pressure; it can cause cuts and burns. Failure to follow these instructions may cause serious personal injury. Use the matching service procedure and [diesel fuel-system precautions](#/document/G1693186).

requirements.category: LPG and CNG systems, where applicable

items.name: Qualified people and authorized workshops
items.detail: WARNING: Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) and Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) system service is restricted to qualified personnel and authorized workshops. Qualifications vary by region; observe local laws and legislative directives. Failure to do so may cause serious personal injury or death. Read the [LPG and CNG precautions](#/document/G1693190).

items.name: Dedicated, ventilated work area
items.detail: WARNING: CNG and LPG are highly flammable and toxic when contained in unventilated work areas. Work in a dedicated area with good ventilation and no ignition sources. Failure to do so may cause serious personal injury or death.

items.name: Protection from liquid LPG
items.detail: WARNING: LPG can injure eyes and freeze skin. Always wear personal protective equipment, including safety goggles and gloves, and avoid contact with liquid gas. Failure to do so may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Storage and indoor parking
items.detail: WARNING: Observe local regulations for storing or parking LPG vehicles indoors. Do not park near heat sources, ignition sources or unventilated open pits. Failure to follow these instructions may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Keep tank discharge outside
items.detail: WARNING: LPG is heavier than air and collects in low areas such as drains and work pits. Never discharge a tank inside a building. If possible, discharge tanks beforehand by running the vehicle; any gas discharge must take place outdoors in a well-ventilated, flat area. Accumulated combustible gas can cause a fire or explosion resulting in personal injury or death.

items.name: Paint-drying ovens
items.detail: WARNING: Extreme heat increases CNG or LPG fuel-tank pressure. Remove the fuel tank before using a paint-drying oven at temperatures above 60° C. Failure to do so may release combustible gas and cause personal injury or death in a fire or explosion.

items.name: LPG material safety information
items.detail: WARNING: Always consult the LPG material safety information sheet before servicing an LPG vehicle. Improper handling presents a personal health hazard and may cause serious personal injury or death.

items.name: Qualification and preparation
items.detail: WARNING: Only qualified personnel may service and handle Pyrotechnic Components. Required qualifications vary by region; always observe local laws and legislative directives. Failure to do so may cause serious personal injury or death. Read the [pyrotechnic-device precautions](#/document/G1693191) and use the matching service procedure; these handling precautions are not a complete isolation, removal or deployment procedure.

items.name: Carry and set down a live airbag
items.detail: WARNING: Carry a live airbag with its deployment door, trim cover or tear seam pointing away from your body. Never set it down with that surface facing downward. Incorrect handling may cause serious personal injury if it deploys accidentally.

items.name: Transport a live safety belt inflator
items.detail: WARNING: Before carrying or transporting a live safety belt inflator, install the safety belt buckle bolt hand tight in the inflator tube. Failure to do so may cause serious personal injury during an accidental deployment.

items.name: Controlled SRS deployment
items.detail: WARNING: Deployment of all supplemental restraint system (SRS) devices, including air bags, pretensioners and load limiters, must take place outdoors with all personnel at least 9 meters (30 feet) away. Hearing protection is required because deployment produces a loud report. Failure to follow these precautions may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Protect safety belt webbing
items.detail: WARNING: Do not bleach or re-dye safety belt webbing; doing so can weaken it and increase the risk of serious personal injury or death in a crash.

items.name: After side airbag deployment
items.detail: WARNING: Following a crash with side air bag deployment, replace the seat backrest cover, seat backrest foam and side airbag. Inspect the side-airbag mounting areas for deformation; if damaged, install a new seat backrest frame. Failure to follow these instructions may cause serious personal injury or death in a crash.

items.name: After Safety Canopy or side air curtain deployment
items.detail: WARNING: Install a new headliner and new roof-pillar upper trim panels with attaching hardware whenever the Safety Canopy or side air curtain has deployed. Make sure the headliner carries the word AIRBAG where it meets each roof B-pillar trim panel. Remove and replace any other damaged components or hardware with new parts. Always use new torque-prevailing type J-nuts when installing the Safety Canopy. Failure to do so can cause incorrect deployment and increase the risk of serious personal injury or death in a crash.

items.name: Restraint connector terminals
items.detail: WARNING: Do not repair or service restraint-component connector terminals. If terminals need repair, replace them with the service connector pigtails. Failure to do so can cause incorrect restraint operation and increase the risk of serious personal injury or death in a crash.

items.name: Deployable seat belt components
items.detail: WARNING: Never disassemble or tamper with deployable seat belt components, including pretensioners, load limiters and inflators. Never back probe deployable-device electrical connectors. Tampering or back probing can cause accidental deployment resulting in personal injury or death.

items.name: RCM and other SRS components
items.detail: WARNING: Never tamper with, repair or modify a Restraints Control Module (RCM) or any other Supplemental Restraint System (SRS) component. Doing so can cause incorrect SRS operation and increase the risk of serious personal injury or death in a crash.

items.name: Airbag and curtain connectors
items.detail: WARNING: Never probe electrical connectors on airbag, Safety Canopy or side air curtain assemblies. Probing can cause accidental deployment and increase the risk of serious personal injury or death.

items.name: Keep a connected RCM in its mounting position
items.detail: WARNING: Do not handle, move or change the RCM's original horizontal mounting position while it is connected and the ignition switch is ON. Doing so can accidentally deploy the Safety Canopy and cause serious personal injury or death.

items.name: Keep curtain deployment paths clear
items.detail: WARNING: Do not obstruct or place objects in the deployment path of the Safety Canopy or side air curtain assembly. Never insert any fastener or tie strap around any part of those assemblies or their related interior trim panels. Obstructions or improper attachments can cause incorrect deployment and increase the risk of serious personal injury or death in a crash.

items.name: Keep OCS assemblies together
items.detail: WARNING: Occupant Classification System (OCS) parts are calibrated as an assembly. Replace them only in the configuration in which they are sold; never separate assembly parts. Otherwise, incorrect OCS operation can increase the risk of serious personal injury or death in a crash.

items.name: Keep OCS components clean
items.detail: WARNING: Never allow oil, grease, water or other foreign contaminants on or inside OCS components or electrical connectors. Contamination can cause incorrect OCS operation and increase the risk of serious personal injury or death in a crash.

items.name: RCM and impact-sensor fasteners
items.detail: WARNING: Always tighten RCM fasteners and impact-sensor fasteners, if equipped, to their specified torque. Obtain the values from the matching service procedure. Incorrect tightening can cause incorrect restraint-system operation and increase the risk of personal injury or death in a crash.

items.name: Carry a live curtain assembly
items.detail: WARNING: Carry a live Safety Canopy or side air curtain assembly with its tear seam pointing away from your body. Failure to do so may cause serious personal injury or death during accidental deployment.

items.name: Leave airbag deployment surfaces unpainted
items.detail: WARNING: Do not paint airbag trim covers or deployment doors. Paint can cause incorrect deployment and increase the risk of serious personal injury or death in a crash.

items.name: Handle a live hood actuator
items.detail: WARNING: Hold a live hood actuator around its cylinder, with the mounting bracket up and the cap pointing away from your body. Set it on its side with the cap pointing away from people. Never place anything in front of the cap. Failure to follow these instructions may cause serious personal injury during an accidental deployment.

items.name: After a pedestrian impact
items.detail: WARNING: Inspect the impact-sensor mounting areas for damage. If damaged, install a new bumper cover. Install new pedestrian impact sensors. Failure to follow these instructions may cause serious personal injury or death in a pedestrian impact.

items.name: Pedestrian-protection connector terminals
items.detail: WARNING: Do not repair or service pedestrian-protection-system connector terminals. If terminals need repair, replace them with the service connector pigtails. Incorrect system operation can increase the risk of serious personal injury or death in a pedestrian impact.

items.name: Pedestrian-protection components
items.detail: WARNING: Never tamper with, repair or modify a pedestrian-protection-system component. Doing so can cause incorrect operation and increase the risk of serious personal injury or death in a pedestrian impact.

items.name: Pedestrian-protection pyrotechnic connectors
items.detail: WARNING: Never probe the electrical connectors on pedestrian-protection-system pyrotechnic assemblies. Probing can cause accidental deployment and increase the risk of serious personal injury or death.

items.name: After pyrotechnic deployment
items.detail: WARNING: Do not handle pyrotechnic components immediately after deployment; they are very hot and may carry pyrotechnic residue. Always wear protective gloves, safety glasses and breathing protection to prevent skin contact with or inhalation of residue. Failure to follow these instructions may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: A tire that has been run flat
items.detail: WARNING: Before inflating a tire that has been run flat, remove it from the wheel and inspect it for damage. A damaged tire can fail during inflation and cause serious personal injury. Read the [wheel and tire precautions](#/document/G1693193).

items.name: Match tube-type and tubeless designs
items.detail: WARNING: Never mount tube-type tires on tubeless wheels or tubeless tires on tube-type wheels. An incorrect combination can allow the tire to separate from the wheel and cause serious injury to occupants.

items.name: Cracked wheels
items.detail: WARNING: Deflate the tire on a cracked wheel before removing the wheel from the vehicle. Cracked wheels are dangerous, and failure to follow this instruction may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Retighten after wheel installation
items.detail: WARNING: Retighten wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi) after reinstalling a wheel. For dual rear wheel (DRW) only, retighten a second time within 800 km (500 mi). Wheels can loosen after initial tightening; failure to retighten may cause serious injury to occupants.

items.name: Match tire and wheel sizes
items.detail: WARNING: Always match tire size to wheel size during assembly. An incorrect match can damage the bead or allow the tire to separate from the wheel, causing serious personal injury to the technician or occupants.

items.name: Replace wheels that would need welding or peening
items.detail: WARNING: Do not weld or peen wheels. Install a new wheel if such repairs would be needed. Failure to follow this rule can cause wheel failure and serious personal injury.

edits.text: Before Any Service Work
edits.why: These general precautions are the starting point before selecting the warnings for the particular system and task.

edits.text: Read these general warnings carefully before beginning any repair. Then review the specific system warnings below before working on any listed system.
edits.why: I check the general precautions first, then match the system warnings to the job. That makes this page a useful preparation checklist while the matching workshop procedure supplies the actual service sequence.

edits.text: WARNING: Before performing or receiving service, inspection or maintenance that requires work underneath or around the vehicle, always disable remote start through the vehicle’s Central Display. Open Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup. If remote start remains enabled, someone could remotely start the vehicle at any time. Failure to disable it could cause personal injury or death.
edits.why: Remote-start control is separate from what you are doing beside the vehicle. This setting removes that particular route to an unexpected start before work begins.

edits.text: WARNING: Wear eye and ear protection whenever servicing a vehicle. Failure to do so may cause serious personal injury.
edits.why: Make both forms of protection part of the initial setup, rather than waiting until the work produces debris or noise.

edits.text: WARNING: Wear protective gloves when handling parts or components with pointed or sharp edges. Failure to do so may cause serious personal injury.
edits.why: Check the edges you will handle as well as the component's main surface; a small exposed edge can be the contact point that matters.

edits.text: WARNING: Improper use of chemicals or materials specified in this manual can create a personal health hazard. Always consult the material safety information sheet before using any specified material. Failure to do so may cause serious personal injury.
edits.why: The material's safety information determines its handling precautions and protective equipment. Being named in a repair procedure does not make a chemical harmless.

edits.text: WARNING: Do not work under the hood with a damaged cooling fan; it can separate during operation. With the ignition OFF, inspect every cooling fan for damage, cracks or separation. Replace a damaged fan with a new fan as necessary. Failure to follow these instructions may cause serious personal injury.
edits.why: The cooling fan moves air through the cooling heat exchangers. Here, visible damage is a safety finding that requires a new fan, rather than an invitation to see whether it still runs. Use the matching replacement procedure for that work.

edits.text: WARNING: Cooling fans can run with the ignition off. Disable the fans before working nearby. On electric vehicles, disconnect the charging cable to prevent unexpected fan operation. Failure to follow these instructions may cause personal injury.
edits.why: A stationary fan is only an observation, not proof that it cannot start. Establish the required fan isolation using the matching vehicle service procedure before entering its working area; the charging-cable instruction specifically applies to electric vehicles.

edits.text: WARNING: On vehicles with engine auto start-stop technology, the engine can start automatically while the ignition is on. Switch the ignition off before servicing or working close to rotating engine parts. Failure to do so may result in serious personal injury.
edits.why: I check the ignition state rather than relying on a silent engine: an automatic stop does not mean the engine cannot restart. Cooling fans have a separate hazard and may run with the ignition off; the nearby fan warning still applies.

edits.text: WARNING: Remove the key from the vehicle during service work to prevent another person from starting the engine without authorization. An accidental start during service may result in serious personal injury.
edits.why: Turning the engine off addresses its current state; removing the key also helps prevent someone else from changing that state while work is underway.

edits.text: WARNING: Before lifting the vehicle with a jack, check that the jack can support the vehicle's weight, including cargo and modifications. Identify the correct jacking points in section 100-02 of this manual and position the vehicle on a hard, level surface. After jacking, always support the vehicle with jack stands. Never get underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. Set the parking brake and block every wheel remaining on the ground. Failure to follow these instructions may allow unintended vehicle movement and result in serious personal injury or death.
edits.why: I treat lifting and supporting as separate jobs: the jack raises the vehicle, and jack stands provide the required support afterward. This is a safety overview, not a complete lifting procedure; use the referenced jacking and lifting section for the actual support locations. The warning symbol is not a placement drawing.

edits.text: WARNING: Before raising the vehicle on a hoist, check that the hoist can support the vehicle's weight, including cargo and modifications. Always position the hoist lift arms as shown in section 100-02 of this manual. Do not use the engine to power the drive wheels unless every drive wheel is clear of the ground. Incorrect lift-arm placement or powered drive wheels touching the ground can cause unintended vehicle movement. Failure to follow these instructions may result in serious personal injury or death.
edits.why: Hoist capacity and lift-arm placement answer different questions: whether the equipment can carry the load and whether it supports the vehicle at the correct locations. I use the referenced lifting instructions for placement rather than guessing from a convenient-looking underside surface.

edits.text: WARNING: Removing heavy components, such as an engine, transmission or axle, while the vehicle is on a hoist can create a dangerous weight imbalance. Restrain the vehicle on the hoist with chains or straps to prevent movement. Failure to do so may result in serious personal injury or death.
edits.why: A vehicle's balance changes when a major assembly comes out, much like unloading one end of a seesaw. I account for that change before removal; adequate hoist capacity alone does not address the shifting balance.

edits.text: WARNING: Always secure transmission, transfer case and axle assemblies to their service jack. Avoid obstructions while raising or lowering the jack. An unsecured assembly, or one that strikes an obstruction, can fall off the jack and cause serious personal injury.
edits.why: I check both the restraint and the travel path. Securing the assembly addresses its attachment to the jack; keeping the path clear addresses contact that could dislodge it during movement.

edits.text: WARNING: Always secure an engine, transmission or other heavy component to its support fixture using straps and wooden support blocks. An unsecured assembly can fall from the fixture and cause serious personal injury.
edits.why: The fixture must both support the component and keep it secured; resting a heavy assembly on it is not enough.

edits.text: WARNING: Never support an engine by its intake or exhaust manifolds. The engine can drop suddenly and cause serious personal injury.
edits.why: The manifolds are not permitted engine support points.

edits.text: WARNING: If equipped, turn off (disable) the power running boards before jacking, lifting or placing any object beneath the vehicle. Never put your hand between a power running board and the vehicle. An extended board retracts when the doors close. Failure to observe these instructions may cause serious personal injury.
edits.why: Closing a door can move an extended board while someone is working beneath or beside the vehicle.

edits.text: WARNING: Keep solvents away from ignition sources. Flammable solvents can ignite or explode if handled incorrectly, causing serious personal injury.
edits.why: Solvent handling includes controlling nearby ignition sources.

edits.text: WARNING: Hold flagnuts with tools, never with your fingers. A flagnut can slip or spin unexpectedly as a fastener is removed and injure your fingers.
edits.why: The flag does not guarantee that the nut will stay still as the fastener turns.

edits.text: Before beginning any service or repair, carefully read the linked safety precautions for every system involved. Select the guidance that matches the vehicle's actual equipment.
edits.why: I use these links as a workshop map: identify the system before choosing the route. A reference to a particular fuel, battery or restraint technology does not mean this vehicle has it. These precautions explain hazards and required safeguards; use the matching service procedures for the actual work, including pressure release, lifting, restraint-system preparation and component installation.

edits.text: Before climate control work, read [Climate Control System Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693184) (100-00 General Information, Description and Operation).
edits.why: The hazards depend on what you are opening or handling: refrigerant can injure through cold contact or gas exposure, while heater components can retain heat.

edits.text: Before battery or charging work, read [Battery and Battery Charging Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693181) (100-00 General Information, Description and Operation).
edits.why: Identify the battery technology first. Sulfuric-acid battery precautions and Li-ion precautions address different hazards and must retain their separate scope.

edits.text: Before brake or clutch work, read [Brake and Clutch Systems Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693183) (100-00 General Information, Description and Operation).
edits.why: Clean fluid protects the hydraulic system; controlled dust removal protects the person working on the friction components.

edits.text: Before body repair, read [Body Repair Health and Safety and General Precautions](#/document/G1693182) (100-00 General Information, Description and Operation).
edits.why: Body repair decisions affect more than the finish. Repair location, replacement parts and restraint mountings can determine how the vehicle protects its occupants in another collision.

edits.text: Before cooling-system work, read [Engine Cooling System Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693187) (100-00 General Information, Description and Operation).
edits.why: The pressure cap is a pressure boundary: even a small turn can release steam and hot coolant while the system is hot.

edits.text: Before gasoline or gasoline-ethanol fuel-system work, read [Gasoline and Gasoline-Ethanol Fuel Systems Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693188) (100-00 General Information, Description and Operation).
edits.why: An engine that has stopped can still leave pressurized fuel behind. The required preparation addresses pressure, temperature, ignition sources and cleanup before restarting.

edits.text: For work on a diesel fuel system, read [Diesel Fuel System Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693186) (100-00 General Information, Description and Operation).
edits.why: This reference applies to diesel equipment; it addresses the separate cutting and burning hazards of high-pressure, hot fuel.

edits.text: For work involving Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) or Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) equipment, read [Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) and Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) Fuel Systems Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693190) (100-00 General Information, Description and Operation).
edits.why: These systems require qualified personnel and authorized workshops. Their precautions also govern ventilation, parking, gas discharge and heat exposure.

edits.text: Before servicing or handling pyrotechnic devices, read [Pyrotechnic Device Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693191) (100-00 General Information, Description and Operation).
edits.why: Live devices need controlled handling, and their connectors are subject to explicit probing prohibitions. Post-collision replacement rules also protect the system's ability to deploy correctly later.

edits.text: Before wheel or tire work, read [Wheel and Tire Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693193) (100-00 General Information, Description and Operation).
edits.why: The precautions cover damage hidden after running flat, compatible assemblies, prohibited wheel repairs and the retightening required after installation.

referenceReview.editorialRevision: Requirements-only removal of ten repeated system-safety groups; first eleven more detailed groups retained unchanged, all primary edits and source references preserved.
